providers.title: The commutant of one operator
providers.scope: {S}' is a weakly and strongly closed unital algebra, different from B(H) unless S is a scalar; it is transitive exactly when S has no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hyperinvariant projections
providers.scope: The projection onto a hyperinvariant subspace of T lies in every von Neumann algebra containing T.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Weighted shifts and weighted sequence spaces
providers.scope: A bilateral weighted shift with weights in (0,1] is unitarily equivalent to right translation on l^2(w) for a positive decreasing w, tails to tails; bounded functionals and annihilators of l^2(w).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Greatest convex minorant
providers.scope: For f_0 = 0 and f_n in [0, infinity], finite infinitely often and above a convex G with G_n/n -> infinity: the greatest convex minorant is finite, its differences tend to infinity, and it equals f at infinitely many contact indices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The root condition
providers.scope: If log w is convex on j <= 0 and concave on j >= 0 and sum over j != 0 of w_j^(1/j) is finite, the ratios w_(j+1)/w_j are summable.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Support separation (Domar)
providers.scope: w positive and decreasing, log w convex on j <= 0 and concave on j >= 0, the root condition, and limsup log w_(-n)/n^2 > log 3 or liminf log w_n/n^2 < -log 3; nonzero b, c with (c_j w_j) and (b_j/w_j) bounded and sum_j b_j c_(j-r) = 0 for r >= 1: max supp b <= min supp c.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Invariant subspaces of weighted translations (Domar, l^2 case)
providers.scope: The same hypotheses on w: the closed invariant subspaces of right translation on l^2(w) are exactly the tails.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Weighted shifts whose invariant subspaces are tails
providers.scope: Logarithmic weights a_j nondecreasing for j >= 0 and for j <= -1 away from the centre, with a_j >= kappa(j+1) for j >= 0 and a_j >= kappa|j| for j <= -1, kappa > 2 log 3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The odometer
providers.scope: Binary digit sequences with the fair-coin product measure and x -> x + 1: residue classes generate the sigma-algebra; the odometer is bimeasurable, measure preserving and ergodic; L^2 is separable and infinite-dimensional.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Decomposable operators
providers.scope: An essentially bounded measurable field of operators on l^2(Z) defines an operator on L^2(X x Z) commuting with the scalar multipliers; products and adjoints act fibrewise.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fields from scalar multipliers
providers.scope: Every operator on L^2(X x Z) that commutes with all scalar multipliers is given by an almost everywhere unique measurable field of operators, bounded by its norm; a projection has projection fibres.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The fibres
providers.scope: With c = 10 and D = 100, every fibre shift S_x has norm e^(-10) and exactly the tails as closed invariant subspaces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The power estimate
providers.scope: ||S^n|| <= exp(-10 floor((n+1)^2/4)) for n >= 1; S is nonzero, quasinilpotent and not a scalar.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two-ended drift
providers.scope: For x not eventually constant, under x -> x + 1 the logarithmic weights on [0, n) gain at least Dn - C(x) and those on [-q, 0) lose at least Dq - C(x).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Decay of the intertwining coefficients
providers.scope: The solution of the commutation recursion decays at both ends of the integer line, because D > c.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The backward intertwiner
providers.scope: A contraction V commuting with S that carries the fibre over x to the fibre over x + 1 and each tail K_(>=h) onto a dense subspace of K_(>=h-1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Strict descent
providers.scope: A measurable label with values in Z or +-infinity that strictly decreases along an ergodic invertible measure-preserving map, -infinity being absorbing, is almost everywhere -infinity or almost everywhere +infinity.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Common invariant subspaces
providers.scope: S, V and the scalar multipliers have no common closed invariant subspace except 0 and H_0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The direct model (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Fibre classification, ||S^n|| <= exp(-10 floor((n+1)^2/4)), the backward intertwiner, and transitivity of the unital algebra generated by S, V and the scalar multipliers.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The hyperinvariant subspace problem (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space carries a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace; its commutant is a proper weakly closed unital transitive algebra.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Invariant subspaces of S and the multipliers
providers.scope: They are the spaces of fields with values in K_(>=sigma(x)) for measurable sigma; only the trivial ones are V-invariant.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Polar conjugates
providers.scope: Finitely many polar conjugates of |S| generate an atomic abelian von Neumann algebra; all of them generate L^infinity(X x Z), which has no minimal projection.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
